# Database fixture from before package extraction

`database.sql`, `expected.json`, and `requests.json` were generated by sending synthetic HTTP requests to an isolated Worker at revision `adb92a6b829477d36bda8301f05da7278372258e`, before the server package was extracted. No production database, real tokens, or user prompts were used. The Worker's database ID, name, tokens, and origin were replaced with example values, and the same persisted D1 database was connected to the new package Worker for verification.

The fixture preserves the migration ledger for the five existing SQL migrations, generic working/waiting/ended sessions, concurrent Devin waits, read tracking, mute and language settings, device registration, and hook revision. The SHA256 in `expected.json` pins the SQL fixture itself. `npm run test:upgrade` restores this fixture and verifies that applying the package's SQL makes no changes and that queries and subsequent ingestion continue from existing cursors.

Do not regenerate expectations from the current package to make them match. `scripts/verify-upgrade.mjs --capture-legacy <isolated-legacy-worker>` is an explicit tool for creating a new baseline from a previous implementation with recorded provenance. This option replaces the target directory's Wrangler configuration with local example values, so always point it at a separate temporary copy.
